observation.visible_scene: A fixed wide shot of a calm coastal beach at low sun. A mirror-smooth wet sand / shallow water surface fills the foreground and lower half, reflecting a heavily clouded sky tinged pink and orange near the horizon. On the right, a dark conifer tree line and a small pinkish building sit on a pebbly shore; a few isolated stones protrude from the wet surface at left and center. The horizon runs across the middle with a warm yellow glow on the left.
visible_changes: The cloud layer slowly drifts and reshapes over the ~2.7 s segment: the dark central cloud mass and the pink-tinged clouds on the right change form and shift position relative to the frame edges.
The reflection on the wet surface changes in lockstep with the sky, so the mirrored cloud patterns deform and move while the mirrored tree line stays put.
The warm glow along the left/center horizon gradually brightens and broadens, and a small brighter spot (sun-like) becomes distinguishable near the horizon around the middle-to-late frames.
Foreground rocks, the tree line, the building, and the waterline remain at fixed pixel positions throughout, indicating no camera pan, tilt, or zoom.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the scene is a sunrise or a sunset, and the full trajectory of the horizon glow beyond this excerpt.
The complete lifetime and true speed of the cloud drift, since both ends are arbitrary crop boundaries.
What the bright horizon spot physically is (sun disc vs. a thinning cloud gap) before/after this segment.
uncertain_details: The exact direction of cloud translation is subtle and hard to pin down; most of the visible change is slow deformation/reshaping rather than a clear lateral slide.
Whether the foreground is wet sand, a thin water film, or a shallow tidal pool is not definitively resolvable from the frames.
The apparent brightening of the horizon could be partly exposure/timelapse effect rather than a purely physical light change.
